cf.title: [Patch]Incorrect usage of PageGetFreeSpace instead of PageGetHeapFreeSpace in heap_xlog_visible

input.subject: [Patch][Bug] Incorrect usage of PageGetFreeSpace instead of PageGetHeapFreeSpace in heap_xlog_visible

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. The patch replaces one function call in heap_xlog_visible so that standby redo records the same FSM value the primary does, and PG 19 already has the fix per message #1. The remaining points are back-patch details: the branch range, the PG 18 variant, and the rebase CFbot asks for. Confidence is medium because only one message is visible and no code was read.

brief.title: Use PageGetHeapFreeSpace in heap_xlog_visible on back branches
brief.problem: On a standby, heap_xlog_visible computes FSM free space with PageGetFreeSpace, which ignores the MaxHeapTuplesPerPage limit. A heap page whose line pointers are all used, for example by many HOT redirects, is recorded in the replica FSM as having free space. Users of PG 14 to 18 replicas are affected; the author says PG 19 already fixed this in a881cc9.
brief.proposed_design: The patch replaces PageGetFreeSpace with PageGetHeapFreeSpace in heap_xlog_visible, so redo reports 0 free space when no new tuple fits. The patch targets PG 14 to 17. PG 18 needs an adjusted version because the function moved to heapam_xlog.c, and the author points to a version in the earlier thread.
author_claims: The bug is an oversight in commit ab7dbd6.
heap_xlog_visible is the only place that uses PageGetFreeSpace for heap pages.
The patch is already fixed in PG 19 by a881cc9 and is not relevant there.
In the test case, without the fix, the master shows 0 free space and the replica about 1150 bytes; with the fix, both show 0.
The mismatch is rarely seen in practice.
brief.thread_state: Only the first message is visible, and nobody has replied. CFbot reports that the patch needs a rebase, and the entry moved to a later CommitFest without review.
unclear: The material does not say what an inserter on a promoted standby does with the wrong FSM entry, beyond needing to recheck and update it.
No PG 18 patch is attached to this thread; the adjusted version exists only in the earlier thread.
The CommitFest target is 14, but the material does not say whether the fix should go to all branches from 14 to 18.
The test case is a shell script in a zip, not a regression or TAP test for the tree.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: The patch changes the free space value that heap_xlog_visible writes to the standby FSM during redo.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The fix targets back branches only, PG 14 to 17, with a separate variant needed for PG 18.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Should the fix go to all branches from 14 to 18, and can a PG 18 patch be attached to this thread?
Against which branch does the attached patch apply, given that CFbot reports it needs a rebase?
What does an inserter on a promoted standby do with the wrong FSM entry, and what does that cost in practice?
Can the shell test case become a TAP test, or is the fix meant to go in without a test?

committability.owner_note: A committer who knows heap redo and the free space map would have to own it; nobody has replied in the visible thread.
committability.liability: A one-call change in heap redo on five back branches, shipped in minor releases. The FSM value is a hint, so the risk is small, but a back-patched redo change stays with the committer.
committability.author_follow_up: No sign either way; the author posted once, split this from an earlier thread, and has not yet posted a rebase.

priority.reason: Message #1 calls the mismatch rare, and it affects only standbys with heap pages at the MaxHeapTuplesPerPage limit. The patch is a one-call change in heapam.c, but nobody has replied and the entry moved CommitFests without review.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so the claim that heap_xlog_visible is the only heap caller of PageGetFreeSpace is unchecked. The PG 18 variant and the cost of the extra line-pointer check during redo could not be judged.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Avoid the creation of the free space map for small heap relations".
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Avoid the creation of the free space map for small heap relations".
Reverted commit(s): Improve code comments in b0eaa4c51b.; Avoid creation of the free space map for small heap relations, take 2.; During pg_upgrade, conditionally skip transfer of FSMs.; Add more tests for FSM.; Clear the local map when not used.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This feature was using a process local map to track the first few blocks
in the relation.  The map was reset each time we get the block with enough
freespace.  It was discussed that it would be better to track this map on
a per-relation basis in relcache and then invalidate the same whenever
vacuum frees up some space in the page or when FSM is created.  The new
design would be better both in terms of API design and performance.

List of commits reverted, in reverse chronological order:

06c8a5090e  Improve code comments in b0eaa4c51b.
13e8643bfc  During pg_upgrade, conditionally skip transfer of FSMs.
6f918159a9  Add more tests for FSM.
9c32e4c350  Clear the local map when not used.
29d108cdec  Update the documentation for FSM behavior..
08ecdfe7e5  Make FSM test portable.
b0eaa4c51b  Avoid creation of the free space map for small heap relations.

precedents_retrieved.title: Deletion of the recycled future WAL files to free-up disk space if max_wal_size is reduced or wal_recycle is set to off
precedents_retrieved.summary: When max_wal_size is reduced or wal_recycle is set to off, a checkpoint should delete recycled future WAL files to free disk space. The author suggested keeping recycled WAL files in a sorted list and, at checkpoint, deleting them from the newest end, rebuilding the list after restart if needed.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No patch was ever posted, so the commitfest entry had nothing to review. Jacob Champion closed it for that reason and invited the author to reopen it if a patch existed. Justin Pryzby supported the idea, and Tom Lane questioned only whether the behaviour was real.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:

of this thread, so I don't think there's anything to review.

precedents_retrieved.title: Better tracking of free space during SP-GiST index build
precedents_retrieved.summary: Tom Lane proposed that SP-GiST index build track several recently used pages per page category instead of only the last one, so that free space is reused better. A fixed table gives more cache slots to leaf pages than to other categories.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No one objected to the patch, and Tomas Vondra called it a solid improvement. After review, Tom Lane planned to make page selection by free space more efficient. He did not have time for that before the commitfest ended, so he asked for the entry to be marked returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I doubt I will get to it this week, so let's mark it RWF for this fest.

precedents_retrieved.title: Skip all-visible pages during second HeapScan of CIC
precedents_retrieved.summary: During the second heap scan of create index concurrently, the patch checks the visibility map and skips all-visible pages, because tuples inserted after the first scan can only be on pages with the VM bit unset. Its safety rests on VM bits being set only by VACUUM, which conflicts with CIC on the relation lock.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund objected that the correctness of CIC should not depend on VM bits never being set concurrently under the SUE lock, since setting them in more places is a goal. Alternatives followed (a lock to detect a running CIC, or snapshot management to stop all-visible from being set), but the thread reached no design, so the author offered to withdraw the patch and it was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Thus I really don't want to
base the correctness of CIC - a relatively infrequent operation - on the
assumption that no VM bits can be set concurrenty due to the SUE lock.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Add redo LSN to pgstats files"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Add redo LSN to pgstats files"
Reverted commit(s): Add redo LSN to pgstats files
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit b860848232aa, that was added as a prerequisite for
the support of pgstats data flush across checkpoints, linking a pgstats
file to a specific checkpoint redo LSN.

As reported, this is proving to be currently problematic when going
through a pg_upgrade, that does direct manipulations of the control file
in the new cluster.  The LSN stored in the pgstats file is not able to
cope with any changes done in the control file by pg_upgrade yet,
causing the pgstats file to be discarded when starting the new cluster
after overriding its redo LSN (one is a `pg_resetwal -l` where the new
cluster's start LSN is bumped by a hardcoded value of 8 segments, see
copy_xact_xlog_xid).

The least painful path going forward is likely going to be a refactor of
the pgstats code so as it is possible to read and write some of its data
with some routines in src/common/, so as pg_upgrade or pg_resetwal are
able to update its data.  The main point is that we are going to need a
LSN in the stats file should we make it written at checkpoint time and
not only as part of a shutdown sequence.  It is too late to dive into
these details for v18, so let's revert the change, and let's try to
figure out all the details in the next release cycle.  The pgstats file
is currently only written as part of a shutdown sequence, and its
contents are still lost on crash, same as older releases.

Bump PGSTAT_FILE_FORMAT_ID.

precedents_retrieved.title: Write visibility map during CLUSTER/VACUUM FULL
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make CLUSTER and VACUUM FULL write the visibility map during heap rewrite, by having rewriteheap.c build VM pages alongside heap pages (bypassing the buffer manager) and flush them to smgr. It used its own simplified all-visible check, relying on HeapTupleSatisfiesVacuum() having already set hint bits; TOAST relations were left without a VM.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund objected to copying visibility-map implementation details into rewriteheap.c and to adding another copy of visibility-determination logic, which he said has proven hard to get right. He also questioned part of the motivation and pointed to related prior discussion that might share logic, especially for TOAST. The author did not respond to these comments for over two months, and the entry was marked returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I don't think we should have yet another copy of logic determining
visibility. It has repeatedly proven hard to get right in the past, and
it'll not get better by having yet another copy.

precedents_retrieved.title: Write visibility map during CLUSTER/VACUUM FULL
precedents_retrieved.authors: Alexander Korotkov (smagen), Justin Pryzby (justinpryzby), Anna Akenteva (anna.akenteva), Anna Akenteva (a.akenteva)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes CLUSTER and VACUUM FULL write the visibility map in heapam_relation_copy_for_cluster(), so the table needs no extra VACUUM afterwards. VM pages are built in RewriteStateData beside the heap pages and written straight to smgr, with an all-visible check that assumes tuples already passed HeapTupleSatisfiesVacuum().
precedents_retrieved.objection: The original author stopped responding, and no one took ownership of the patch. In 2019 the entry was returned with feedback because review comments went unanswered for more than two months. After a 2021 revival, Justin Pryzby kept rebasing it and asked for an owner, then proposed closing it, and the entry was marked returned with feedback in 2022. Open points included Amit Kapila's question about syncing VM pages at end_heap_rewrite and Justin Pryzby's note that pg_class.relallvisible is not set.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I'm planning to close this patch until someone can shepherd it.

precedents_retrieved.title: Adding TRIM_SPACE option to COPY
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a boolean TRIM_SPACE option to COPY FROM, for FORMAT text and csv, that strips leading and trailing spaces from each column value before NULL processing and type conversion. The option is modeled on a similar Snowflake feature and on existing COPY options such as FORCE_NULL.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the option adds processing cost to every COPY, used or not, and that COPY should not become a general-purpose filter or ETL tool. Fujii Masao then suggested that only features hard to build outside core belong in COPY, and noted that trimming can be done with COPY PROGRAM. The author offered to withdraw if the general view was that the feature should stay external, and the entry was withdrawn.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
COPY is not a general-purpose filter or ETL tool, and we try
to make it one at our peril.

precedents_retrieved.title: Pruning never visible changes
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Tom Lane, Greg Stark, Alvaro Herrera
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets heap pruning remove a committed tuple version that no other transaction could ever see, such as a row inserted and then updated in the same transaction. It removes such a tuple only when xmin equals xmax and the tuple is at the root of the HOT chain.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane said a safe version must check that the originating transaction has no snapshots that can still see the older row version, and doubted it would fire often enough to be worth the cost. Greg Stark pointed to commit 44e4bbf75d, which removed the same xmin == xmax special case because VACUUM could remove TOAST tuples that MVCC-safe CLUSTER still needs. Alvaro Herrera asked whether the patch was safe given that TOAST problem, and Simon Riggs agreed to replace it with a test case and a comment explaining why such rows cannot be removed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
But this begs the question: is the proposed change safe, given that
ancient consideration?  I don't think TOAST issues have been mentioned
in this thread so far, so I wonder if there is a test case that verifies
that this problem doesn't occur for some reason.

precedents_retrieved.title: COPY FREEZE and PD_ALL_VISIBLE
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make COPY FREEZE set PD_ALL_VISIBLE on the pages it fills, so the first VACUUM does not have to rewrite the whole table. The patch sets the flag when hio extends the relation and does not clear it on insert; creating the visibility map file was left open.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No reviewer objected to the patch. Simon Riggs said he was working on a new version that builds the visibility map during the copy, so Amit Kapila marked the entry "Waiting on Author". No new version came, and Michael Paquier returned it with feedback for lack of author input.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
There has not been an update for this patch in a while, switched to
"returned with feedback" because of lack of author's input.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert changes in HOT handling of BRIN indexes
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert changes in HOT handling of BRIN indexes
Reverted commit(s): Ignore BRIN indexes when checking for HOT udpates; Move test for BRIN HOT behavior to stats.sql
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commits 5753d4ee32 and fe60b67250 that modified HOT to
ignore BRIN indexes. The commit message for 5753d4ee32 claims that:

    When determining whether an index update may be skipped by using
    HOT, we can ignore attributes indexed only by BRIN indexes. There
    are no index pointers to individual tuples in BRIN, and the page
    range summary will be updated anyway as it relies on visibility
    info.

This is partially incorrect - it's true BRIN indexes don't point to
individual tuples, so HOT chains are not an issue, but the visibitlity
info is not sufficient to keep the index up to date. This can easily
result in corrupted indexes, as demonstrated in the hackers thread.

This does not mean relaxing the HOT restrictions for BRIN is a lost
cause, but it needs to handle the two aspects (allowing HOT chains and
updating the page range summaries) as separate. But that requires a
major changes, and it's too late for that in the current dev cycle.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found in the list. Message #1 says this spins off an earlier thread on a related second issue and that PG 19 already fixed it in a881cc9; the material reports no rejection there. A one-line back-branch bug fix gives no prior-rejection reason to apply.

Nothing objectionable from the standards and compatibility angle. The fix changes only the free space value that redo writes to the standby FSM. It adds no syntax, GUC, catalog object, psql behaviour or pg_dump content, and it does not change what clients see. The back-branch FSM value is a hint, and redo on unpatched standbys still behaves as it does today. The angle cannot check whether the FSM value changes plans or other behaviour on existing branches, because the code is not shown.

The fix changes only the value that redo writes to the standby FSM, and the FSM is advisory, so inserters recheck the page. It adds no WAL record, on-disk format, catalog or ABI change, so it is safe to backpatch and to run in mixed minor versions. Stale FSM entries left on existing standbys correct themselves on later updates.

The patch changes how WAL redo on a standby computes the free space it records in the FSM for a heap page. It adds no privilege, role, setting, or interface, and it exposes no data to any user, so there is nothing to object to from the security angle. A stale FSM entry only costs an inserter a recheck, and the patch makes that less likely.

No objection from the maintenance angle. The patch swaps one function call in heap_xlog_visible to match what every other heap code path already does, adds no state, API or mechanism, and only costs a line-pointer check during redo of visibility records. The PG 18 variant and the branch range are back-patch details for the committer to settle.

This is a back-branch bug fix to an existing redo path. No existing feature, extension or tool gives standby redo the correct FSM value, so there is nothing to point to as an alternative. The fix uses the existing PageGetHeapFreeSpace and adds no new mechanism.

This is a one-line bug fix that makes back branches match the heap free-space rule already used on master. A demand test does not apply, and the cost falls on nobody. Low field impact (message #1 calls the mismatch rare) is a question of back-patch priority, which other panel members can weigh better than the demand angle.
